entries.text: A blueprint name can only be used once.

provenance.quote: blueprint names have to be unique

entries.text: Allocating from a blueprint gives two allocations per TYPE_A requirement set and one per other set.
entries.predicate:
fun t =>
  match t.action.cmd, t.out.body with
  | .alCreate n, .allocations as =>
    match t.before.blueprints.find? (·.name == n) with
    | some b => as.length == (b.sets.map multiplicity).sum
    | none => false
  | _, _ => true

provenance.quote: a TYPE_A set should give two allocations, everything else one

entries.text: A bind that adds to an assignment only succeeds if nothing is bound to it yet.
entries.predicate:
fun t =>
  match t.action.cmd, t.out.body with
  | .alBind a ops _, .accepted =>
    !ops.any (·.2 == .add) || !t.before.allocations.any (fun al => al.status == "bound" && al.assignment == some a)
  | _, _ => true

provenance.quote: once an assignment has allocations bound you can't bind more to it
if a bind or a delete fails, nothing should have changed

entries.text: An allocation is bound exactly when it has an assignment.
entries.predicate: fun t => t.after.allocations.all fun a => (a.status == "bound") == a.assignment.isSome

provenance.quote: bound means it has an assignment, unbound means it doesn't

entries.text: The ledger lists exactly the capabilities of the active units.

provenance.quote: the ledger should show what the active units can do, nothing more

entries.text: A module has at most one tag per key.

provenance.quote: one tag per key on a module

entries.text: Blueprint create and delete never succeed in system scope.

provenance.quote: system scope must never create or delete blueprints

entries.predicate: fun t => t.after.allocations.all fun a => t.after.blueprints.any (·.name == a.blueprint)

provenance.quote: don't let a blueprint be deleted while allocations still use it

entries.text: Binding never moves an allocation that is bound to another assignment.
entries.predicate:
fun t =>
  match t.action.cmd, t.out.body with
  | .alBind a ops _, .accepted =>
    ops.all fun (id, op) => op != .add ||
      (t.before.allocations.find? (·.id == id)).all fun al => al.status != "bound" || al.assignment == some a
  | _, _ => true

provenance.quote: binding should never steal an allocation from another assignment
